Package edu.cnu.mdi.undo

Class ItemEdits

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.undo.ItemEdits
public final class ItemEdits extends Object
Factories for the undoable edits an interactive container records: changing items' state (move, resize, rotate, restyle, edit text), creating an item, and deleting items. Each is a UndoableEdit for a UndoManager.

Deletion keeps the item alive

Undoable deletion takes an item out of its layer (Layer.detach(AItem)) but does not dispose it, so undoing puts back the very same object with its geometry, style and identity intact. The item is disposed (AItem.prepareForRemoval()) only when its edit leaves the history for good, such as when the history is cleared or trimmed to its limit, so nothing leaks. Creation works the same way in reverse: undoing a creation detaches the new item and keeps it for redo.

All edits must be made and undone on the Swing event thread.

      public static UndoableEdit changedStates(String name, IContainer container, List<? extends AItem> items, List<ItemState> before)
      Builds the edit that takes the items from the given earlier states to their current states, leaving out items that cannot be snapshotted and items that did not change.
      Parameters:
      name - the edit's name as shown in an Undo menu, such as "Move"
      container - the container to repaint after undo/redo
      items - the items, in the same order as before
      before - the states captured earlier with capture(java.util.List<? extends edu.cnu.mdi.item.AItem>)
      Returns:
      the edit, or null if nothing changed

      Builds the edit for an item that has just been created on its layer. Undoing detaches the item and keeps it for redo.

    • delete

      public static UndoableEdit delete(IContainer container, List<? extends AItem> items)
      Deletes the items from their layers undoably and returns the edit that brings them back. The items are detached, not disposed (see the class description).
      Parameters:
      container - the container to repaint after undo/redo
      items - the items to delete; each is deleted from its own layer
      Returns:
      the edit, or null if none of the items was on a layer
